questionText:
Consider the following C code:

The code suffers from which one of the following problems:
options: compiler error as the return of malloc is not typecast appropriately
compiler error because the comparison should be made as x == NULL and not as shown
compiles successfully but execution may result in dangling pointer
compiles successfully but execution may result in memory leak
explanation:
1. Compilation Check:
• In C, void* returned by malloc is implicitly converted to any pointer type, so explicit typecasting is not mandatory.
• The comparison NULL == x is syntactically valid in C.
Hence, the code compiles without any compilation error.

2. Memory Leak Analysis:
• First allocation: int *x = malloc(sizeof(int)); allocates dynamic memory block $M_1$ and stores its address in pointer $x$.
• Inside the if(x) block: x = (int *)malloc(sizeof(int)); allocates a new memory block $M_2$ and reassigns pointer $x$ to point to $M_2$.
• The memory address of block $M_1$ is lost without being freed.
• Because block $M_1$ can no longer be accessed or deallocated, it causes a memory leak.

Therefore, the code compiles successfully but execution may result in a memory leak.
